author: gpt-5.6-luna
kind: a release-train calendar (a new release every 6 weeks, each branching from main 6 weeks before release), throughput history for the last 12 sprints (CSV), a remaining-work export (CSV, 60 to 100 tickets, some unestimated, some split into sub-tickets) and a doc describing the review and stabilisation rules
scenario: A director asks: which release will the new storage engine ship in? Give me the one I can promise customers, and the one we will most likely make.
seeds: (1) the work must merge before a branch date, not the release date; (2) throughput history has one outlier sprint (a hackathon) that inflates the mean; (3) about 15% of remaining tickets are unestimated and the doc gives a rule for sizing them from history; (4) a stabilisation rule says a feature must sit behind a flag for one full train before being on by default, which moves the promise by one train; (5) a decoy: a big ticket labelled storage that belongs to a different feature.
expertSources: The Rust Book, How Rust is Made and Nightly Rust, https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/appendix-07-nightly-rust.html (MIT OR Apache-2.0)
PEP 745, Python 3.14 Release Schedule, https://peps.python.org/pep-0745/ (public domain or CC0-1.0)
